chief_complaint: Obesity and metabolic syndrome with hypertension and early diabetic kidney disease
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 50‑year‑old Hispanic male with a long‑standing history of severe obesity (BMI ≥40) diagnosed in 1995. Metabolic syndrome was documented in 2014, and essential hypertension began in 2010, currently treated with a triple antihypertensive regimen (lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, amlodipine). Prediabetes was identified in 2007 and is being managed with insulin despite a markedly low HbA1c of 3.3%, raising concern for overtreatment. Anemia has been present since 2010. In September 2022, stage 1 chronic kidney disease and diabetic kidney disease were recorded. Socially, the patient transitioned from full‑time/part‑time employment to being not in the labor force in late 2022, coinciding with the emergence of CKD. Recent vital signs show a low normal blood pressure (100/57 mmHg) and heart rate 80 bpm. Key laboratory data (eGFR, lipid panel, albuminuria) are missing, limiting precise risk stratification.
